page: Microsoft Azure D192ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 192 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 96 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 480 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. It also features a bundled local NVMe SSD storage capacity of 11339 GB, while containing no GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, Passmark CPU scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, registering top-tier results for both cached small-block reads and uncached large-block read and write operations. Single-core performance is moderate, placing in the middle 50% for stress-ng single-core tests. The processor's advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions), support accelerated vector and matrix operations.

This server is highly optimized for resource-dense workloads that benefit from massive parallel processing and high-speed local storage. It demonstrates top-tier performance in database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput. It is also capable of handling large-scale LLM prompt processing, though text generation speeds for smaller models are relatively weak. Given its massive vCPU count, high memory capacity, and substantial local NVMe storage, the D192ds_v7 offers high qualitative cost efficiency for enterprise databases, heavy ETL pipelines, and high-throughput web serving environments.
